instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tilted your head to judge that cupboard door, so I've tilted mine. It's still crooked. Give me the screwdriver.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm looking under the hinge for the screw I dropped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, underneath first. You find it; I'll take over the door while you're down there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. Hand me the screwdriver and I'll keep the door attached while you take the credit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've circled two names together, so I've circled the exes. They shouldn't share a table. Give me the seating-plan pencil.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those circles mean food allergies, not couples. The exes aren't together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, food first. I'll put them at separate tables with their own meals clearly marked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already done that. This took me hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me check each table against your list. You can keep the list; give me the pencil and I'll make any changes on the plan.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your umbrella back, open like you leave yours. It'll be ready for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only leave it open to dry. Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, drying first. I gave it a rinse. I'll wipe the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll rinse that out too. Have your breakfast; I'll get it dry and back in the stand before you need it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Side plates, yes. I've stood this one on its side in the cupboard. It's back for Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Side means small. That one's large, and it's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A small flourish, exactly. I'll take that plate; the potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want six matching plates, not five plain ones and that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more like this before lunch. Keep the plain ones as spares; we needn't sort through those today.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've held that spoon up to the light, so I've checked mine the same way. Is it bright enough for Mum's lunch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was checking my reflection. You still haven't cleaned the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, reflections matter. Could you check the forks while I polish this one? Mum notices cutlery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've asked her to bring gloves and help you clean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need a guest towel. Help me find one without a faded stripe; I want it ready when she takes the gloves off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put a red label on your box, so I've put red on all mine. Should I underline the names too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Red means fragile. Your boxes haven't even been packed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, fragile contents. We need clear writing before anything goes in. Is that underline thick enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The moving van's outside. We need to fill the boxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take this label out to the man first. Ask if he can read it from the van; I don't want our things going to the wrong room.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The plumber said isolate it, so I've closed the bathroom door. You've been working all night; sit down and I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He meant turn off the water. It's coming under the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, the water next. Just a little drying to do. Take the sofa; I'll put a tray there for you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll find the stopcock before I sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me which cupboard it's in and keep your feet up. I'll do that and bring the tray; you're not spending your morning on the floor.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put a star beside Friday, so I've added two beside Saturday. Is this how we're choosing the picnic day?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The star means read the note. The picnic's on Friday now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the note. Is that your blue pen it's written in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I moved it because I'm working Saturday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That explains it. Who's telling the guests who booked Saturday off? Shall I put their names under your note?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm doing yoga. There's room since the table moved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, flexibility. Did making this room involve you moving the table?

beats.speaker: A
